record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Can one prove an approximation theorem for the vacuum Einstein equations: if an approximate metric g_epsilon has Ricci curvature bounded by epsilon in a suitable norm, then there exists an exact Ricci-flat metric g within epsilon of g_epsilon in a suitable norm?

evidence.quote: Prove any result of the form: Conjecture: Let ge be an "approximate solut~on" of the (vacuum) Einstein equations (i.e. IIRic(ge)ll :s; e, in some suitable norm). Then there is a metric g such that Ric(g) = 0 and Ug-gell :S: e .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold (compact, or with suitable asymptotic conditions imposed at infinity), and let $\mathrm{Ric}(g)$ denote the Ricci curvature tensor of a Lorentzian (or Riemannian) metric $g$ on $M$. Call a metric $g_\varepsilon$ on $M$ an "approximate vacuum solution" if $\|\mathrm{Ric}(g_\varepsilon)\| \le \varepsilon$, measured in some suitable norm (for instance a weighted Hölder or Sobolev norm appropriate to the geometric setting).

Establish a theorem of the following form, or determine the appropriate hypotheses under which it holds:

There exist constants $\varepsilon_0 > 0$ and $C > 0$, and choices of norms $\|\cdot\|_A$, $\|\cdot\|_B$, such that for every metric $g_\varepsilon$ on $M$ with $\|\mathrm{Ric}(g_\varepsilon)\|_A \le \varepsilon < \varepsilon_0$ (and satisfying any necessary non-degeneracy/structural conditions), there exists an exact Ricci-flat metric $g$ on $M$ (i.e. $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = 0$) such that
$$\|g - g_\varepsilon\|_B \le C\,\varepsilon.$$

Identify natural hypotheses (e.g.\ bounds on curvature, injectivity radius, topology, asymptotic structure, gauge fixing) and norms under which such an approximation/stability theorem for the vacuum Einstein equations can be proved, or produce counterexamples showing it fails in general.
artifact.status_search_result: No general approximation theorem of this form for the vacuum Einstein equations has been established. Partial results exist (e.g. stability of Minkowski space, perturbative/linearized gravity, Ricci-flat deformation results near integrable solutions), but the general conjecture as posed remains open and is sensitive to the choice of norms and geometric setting.

status_evidence.title: Einstein field equations - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Vacuum field equations define Einstein manifolds; Ricci-flat metrics.
status_evidence.claim: Context: vacuum Einstein equations correspond to Ricci-flat metrics, the setting of the conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Linearized gravity - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Approximation as Minkowski plus a perturbation; linearized Einstein equations.
status_evidence.claim: Only perturbative/linearized approximation results are standard; no general nonlinear epsilon-approximation theorem is known.
